transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you. Um, well, I came in because I've been dealing with some really awful, unwanted thoughts lately. 

I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt recently—I'm an artist, so I was putting this together for her—and I just kept getting these thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. It was like... like if I made one wrong photo placement, or picked the wrong color choice, it would mean I didn't love her enough. I'm used to having normal creative doubts with my work, but I just couldn't brush these off at all. They really stuck with me, so I figured I needed to come talk to someone about it.

Can you tell me more about these unwanted thoughts? Specifically, do they feel like they’re coming from outside of your usual way of thinking, and do they upset you because they’re inconsistent with how you see yourself?

Um, I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about it quite like that. I don't know if they feel like they come from outside my usual way of thinking... I mean, they are in my head, so they feel like my thoughts, even if I don't want them there. 

And as for being inconsistent with how I see myself, I'm not really sure what you mean by that. I haven't noticed anything like that. I just know they upset me a lot because I loved my aunt, and the idea of messing up her memorial piece just made me feel terrible. I don't really have a better way to explain it.
Do these thoughts feel intrusive, like they don’t really fit with how you normally think, and do you find them disturbing or unacceptable?

I guess... I mean, intrusive is a good word for it, because they just pop in there and I can't get them to stop. But I don't know if they feel like they don't fit how I normally think. They're just... my thoughts, you know? Just really loud, persistent ones. 

And, yeah, I definitely find them disturbing. It's awful to sit there trying to make something beautiful for someone you miss, and your brain is just telling you over and over that you're ruining it and disrespecting them. It's just really upsetting. But I don't know if I'd call them "unacceptable" in the way you're asking. I just want them to go away so I can finish the piece.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking, redoing parts of the memorial piece, or going through certain mental steps—to try to reduce the anxiety these thoughts bring up?

Yeah, I do. Um, I'll end up rereading the label text for the piece, or I'll just keep nudging the same objects on my work table. And I check the layout photos over and over again. I basically just keep doing all that until it finally feels... settled, I guess. 

It's frustrating because a part of me knows it's already fine. Like, logically, I know it looks good, but I keep doing it anyway to try and make that feeling go away, and I end up just losing a lot of my studio time.
Do these unwanted thoughts lead you to feel like you have to perform these checking behaviors, or do the behaviors just help a little with the anxiety without any specific rule or expectation?

Um, I definitely feel like I have to do them. Like I was just saying, it's not like I just check the layout photos or reread the text once to take the edge off. I feel like I have to keep doing it... keep nudging the things on my table... until I get that specific settled feeling. 

It's not necessarily a strict rule, like counting to a certain number, but the rule is basically that I can't stop until it feels right. Even though part of me knows the piece is already fine, I feel forced to keep going until that feeling hits, which is why I just end up losing so much time in the studio.
